rationale: A direct Commission→Member States relation exists for communicate, but seek has the approved laboratory as its addressee. The candidate row improperly fuses actions with different recipients and must be split without losing the conditions stated in Article 8(3).

The approved laboratory occupies a defined technical position in the regulatory procedure: if consultation does not resolve the dispute, the Commission must seek the opinion of an approved laboratory external to the States involved. The intermediary position is derived for this conditional legal configuration only, not as a permanent attribute of every approved laboratory and not as evidence that an opinion was actually issued.

For Article 11(2), the national regulatory authority makes statistical reports available, sends them to the Commission, and provides data on request. The immediately expressed governance function is reporting/information provision. Monitoring may be antecedent activity but should not replace the function directly observable in the provision. Articles 11(1) and 11(2) should remain separate relationships.

Article 5(4) supports a legally possible intermediary position for collecting societies because Member States may regulate whether and to what extent collective administration is imposed. It does not establish that the option was adopted, that a particular society received the administration, or that the intermediary position is effectively instantiated. Record the legal authorization and modality separately; derived effective intermediary status remains unresolved.

Article 7 constitutes an observable legal relation. Commission→committee is directly supported for consult. Committee→Commission assistance/advice is a distinct directional relation and should not be fused into the same primitive edge. The substantive type should remain limited to consultation/advisory assistance without inferring specific tasks not stated in the provision.

Article 3(2) describes bodies notified by each Member State to the other Member States and the Commission. The candidate Member State→body: notify/designate assigns the wrong recipient to notify. Correct first to Member State→other Member States/Commission: notify bodies. A designation edge requires separate legal support.

Article 3(2) waives a declaration when marks or certificates issued by notified bodies are used. It does not establish a direct Member State→manufacturer action of enable use. The legal effect of the exemption must be recorded separately from the candidate actor-to-actor relation.

Neither candidate verb fits the proposed Member State→manufacturer edge. Issue marks/certificates belongs to the notified bodies, while enable use is not expressed as a direct action between the candidate actors. Actor, recipient, and relationship must be corrected before action normalization; if only a verb is allowed, leave action_normalized undecided until the edge is reconstructed.

Civil-liability insurance is a condition imposed on the notified body. The provision does not assign a regulatory function to an insurer. Direct intermediary status is therefore not established by this provision.

The insurance requirement alone does not supply the qualifying relational edges required for a derived intermediary position. A requirement to maintain coverage must not be converted into an R–I–T chain without additional evidence.

Article 10(2) requires Member States to inform the Commission of designated testing laboratories. Inform is directed to the Commission, not the laboratories. Designated characterizes the laboratories; any designation edge requires separate legal support and coding.

Annex III point 3.3 concerns assessment of the quality-control system to determine whether it satisfies the requirements of point 3.2. Point 4 separately governs subsequent surveillance. Assurance is therefore the better function label than continuing monitoring for this provision.

The mechanism in point 3.3 is assessment of the quality system, including inspection visit and reasoned decision. It should not be collapsed into periodic audit/surveillance governed separately in point 4.

The procedural device is the quality-system assessment in point 3.3. The text does mention an auditing team and an inspection visit; the decision does not deny audit-like elements. It distinguishes this assessment procedure from the periodic audit/surveillance regime of point 4.

The candidate Registry→Commission row compresses incompatible relations. Split into Registry→auditor: appoint (after consultation with the Commission), auditor→Registry phased-registration administration/process: audit, and auditor→Commission: report findings. The Registry's responsibility for the audit expense must remain represented and must not disappear in normalization.

Article 14 directly establishes applicant→validation agent: submit documentary evidence. The fact that the validation agent is indicated by the Registry is a separate relation and does not make the applicant's submission duty composite.

The candidate Registry→ADR providers row mixes subjects and directions. Split into Registry→ADR provider: select (Article 23), complainant/respondent→ADR provider: submit complaint/response (Article 22(5)), and ADR provider→Registry: inform (Article 22(6)). Any examine action belongs to the provider and must be linked to the examined object; if it refers to examination of complaint compliance, its specific basis is Article 22(7), not merely paragraphs 5–6.

For the candidate Member State→non-profit organisation line, direct intermediary status is not demonstrated. External audit or supervision by a public authority or self-regulatory body appears as an alternative condition for exemption, not as assignment of that intermediary function to the organisation in the candidate line. This does not preclude a self-regulatory body from being an intermediary in another properly coded relation.

Derived intermediary position is also not established for this candidate line. The enumeration of safeguards does not replace identification and documentation of qualifying edges. Preserve the architectural condition external audit OR public/self-regulatory supervision without declaring a demonstrated intermediary position.
